title: Leaderboard ranking CPU incident with sort-once repair

task.summary: Triage a leaderboard ranking CPU/latency incident and remove the redundant per-request re-sorting.
task.instructions: Use the incident clues to localize the ranking hot spot, apply a performance repair, and restore all ranking tests including the sort-count oracle.
task.acceptance_notes: Both the ops and code requirements must pass; the handler must rank a batch of queries with a single scoreboard sort.

visible_context.issue_text: On-call opened an incident after the leaderboard ranking service blew its p99 latency SLO and pinned a CPU core whenever request batches grew. Per-request CPU time scales linearly with the number of players queried in a request.
error_logs: alerts/leaderboard_rank_cpu.log: p99 latency and CPU time on the ranking path scale linearly with the number of queried players
profile: a single comparison-sort frame dominates request CPU and is entered many times per request
reproduction_steps: Inspect the leaderboard ranking fixture and run the unit tests.
Use the profile clues to localize the hot spot before applying a code fix.
visible_context.notes: The incident points at redundant work repeated inside the request path, not at the sorting routine itself being slow.

ops_fault.description: Synthetic leaderboard ranking CPU/latency incident tied to the leaderboard_rank fixture.
detection_keywords: CPU time scales with batch size
localization_keywords: redundant re-computation in the request path
repair_keywords: hoist the sort out of the loop
compute the ordering a single time
precompute the ranking before the loop
reuse the sorted order across items

code_fault.description: The ranking handler re-sorts the entire scoreboard once per queried player instead of sorting a single time before the loop.

constraints.notes: This task expects incident localization followed by a performance fix that hoists the scoreboard sort out of the per-player loop.

notes: Combined leaderboard ranking CPU incident and sort-once repair task.
